parsed.explanation: Thin-data dossier, but the structural signals are consistent: no sodomy or presentation offence ever existed, no trans-specific criminal law, no documented border, facility, custody or care exposure, and no record of police targeting or violence against trans visitors. Positives: transgender people appear in traditional costume at temples/ceremonies (documented acceptance analogue), diplomatic marking of the international day against homophobia in the capital, and an assembly member's 2025 non-discrimination proposal. Negatives: no SOGI anti-discrimination law, societal discrimination described as prevalent (dated 2013, resident/social sphere), state tolerance conditional on not being publicly 'immodest' or campaigning, blocked LGBTI webpages, media framing trans people as entertainment. None of these is a traveller-facing universal exposure or organised targeting. Absence of violence records is weakly positive given diplomatic monitoring exists. Net: reduced-risk but thin, with open questions on custody placement and document scrutiny.
